cards.front: temperature
cards.back: How hot or cold something is. It is measured in degrees Celsius with a thermometer.
cards.say: temperature. How hot or cold something is. It is measured in degrees Celsius with a thermometer.

cards.front: How does temperature affect how much solid can dissolve?
cards.back: Usually more solid dissolves in warmer water.
cards.say: How does temperature affect how much solid can dissolve? Usually more solid dissolves in warmer water.

cards.front: solubility
cards.back: How much of a substance can dissolve in a liquid at a given temperature.
cards.say: solubility. How much of a substance can dissolve in a liquid at a given temperature.

cards.front: saturated solution
cards.back: A solution in which no more solute can dissolve at that temperature.
cards.say: saturated solution. A solution in which no more solute can dissolve at that temperature.

cards.front: What may happen when a saturated hot solution cools?
cards.back: Some solute comes out of the solution and forms solid crystals.
cards.say: What may happen when a saturated hot solution cools? Some solute comes out of the solution and forms solid crystals.

cards.front: crystal
cards.back: A solid with flat sides and a regular shape, such as a salt or sugar crystal.
cards.say: crystal. A solid with flat sides and a regular shape, such as a salt or sugar crystal.

cards.front: How can you grow crystals?
cards.back: Make a saturated solution in warm water, then let it cool or evaporate slowly.
cards.say: How can you grow crystals? Make a saturated solution in warm water, then let it cool or evaporate slowly.

cards.front: boiling point
cards.back: The temperature at which a liquid boils. For pure water at sea level it is 100 degrees Celsius.
cards.say: boiling point. The temperature at which a liquid boils. For pure water at sea level it is 100 degrees Celsius.

cards.front: boiling
cards.back: When a liquid changes to a gas throughout the liquid, with bubbles of vapour, at its boiling point.
cards.say: boiling. When a liquid changes to a gas throughout the liquid, with bubbles of vapour, at its boiling point.

cards.front: evaporation
cards.back: When a liquid changes to a gas at its surface, at any temperature.
cards.say: evaporation. When a liquid changes to a gas at its surface, at any temperature.

cards.front: What is the main difference between boiling and evaporation?
cards.back: Boiling happens at one temperature and throughout the liquid. Evaporation happens at any temperature and only at the surface.
cards.say: What is the main difference between boiling and evaporation? Boiling happens at one temperature and throughout the liquid. Evaporation happens at any temperature and only at the surface.

cards.front: What are the bubbles in boiling water?
cards.back: Bubbles of water vapour, which is water as a gas.
cards.say: What are the bubbles in boiling water? Bubbles of water vapour, which is water as a gas.

cards.front: What happens to the temperature of water while it boils?
cards.back: It stays at 100 degrees Celsius until all the water has changed to gas.
cards.say: What happens to the temperature of water while it boils? It stays at 100 degrees Celsius until all the water has changed to gas.

cards.front: Name three things that make evaporation faster.
cards.back: Higher temperature, a larger surface area and moving air such as wind.
cards.say: Name three things that make evaporation faster. Higher temperature, a larger surface area and moving air such as wind.

cards.front: Why do wet clothes dry faster on a warm, windy day?
cards.back: Warm, moving air makes the water evaporate faster.
cards.say: Why do wet clothes dry faster on a warm, windy day? Warm, moving air makes the water evaporate faster.

cards.front: melting point of ice
cards.back: Zero degrees Celsius.
cards.say: melting point of ice. Zero degrees Celsius.

cards.front: What is steam?
cards.back: Invisible water vapour. The white cloud you see above a kettle is tiny droplets of liquid water.
cards.say: What is steam? Invisible water vapour. The white cloud you see above a kettle is tiny droplets of liquid water.

cards.front: condensation
cards.back: When a gas cools and changes to a liquid.
cards.say: condensation. When a gas cools and changes to a liquid.

cards.front: Does salt water boil at a higher or lower temperature than pure water?
cards.back: Higher, a little above 100 degrees Celsius.
cards.say: Does salt water boil at a higher or lower temperature than pure water? Higher, a little above 100 degrees Celsius.

cards.front: Why does water boil at a lower temperature on a high mountain?
cards.back: The air pressure is lower, so less heat is needed for the water to boil.
cards.say: Why does water boil at a lower temperature on a high mountain? The air pressure is lower, so less heat is needed for the water to boil.

cards.front: Which dissolves faster in the same amount of water: hot or cold?
cards.back: Hot. Particles move faster and meet the solid more often.
cards.say: Which dissolves faster in the same amount of water: hot or cold? Hot. Particles move faster and meet the solid more often.

cards.front: Does dissolving faster mean more dissolves in total?
cards.back: Not always. Speed of dissolving and the amount that can dissolve are different things.
cards.say: Does dissolving faster mean more dissolves in total? Not always. Speed of dissolving and the amount that can dissolve are different things.

cards.front: You heat salt water until it is boiling. What is left when all the water is gone?
cards.back: The salt, as a solid.
cards.say: You heat salt water until it is boiling. What is left when all the water is gone? The salt, as a solid.

cards.front: What instrument do we use to measure temperature?
cards.back: A thermometer.
cards.say: What instrument do we use to measure temperature? A thermometer.
